note: Identification of a de novo missense variant in TAF4 in a patient with severe DLD and non-verbal IQ >= 70 supports a phenotypic continuum beyond pLoF-associated intellectual disability.

evidence.text: In a prospective cohort of 25 individuals with severe developmental language disorder and no intellectual disability (non-verbal IQ >= 70), a likely pathogenic de novo missense variant in TAF4 was identified in an individual displaying DLD within the spectrum of TAF4-related disorders.

evidence.text: The initial cohort defining TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder described eight individuals all carrying de novo putative loss-of-function variants, with common features including intellectual disability.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.
